events.title: Next Fest is on, and the demo just got its biggest update
events.summary: Pocket Adventurer is in Steam Next Fest this week, and I pushed a demo update tonight to go with it. It's an idle RPG that lives in a thin strip above your Windows taskbar. Your hero runs dungeons down there while you work. Check in whenever. They'll be fine. Probably. What's new in the demo Every menu was rebuilt out of the game's own wood, parchment and gold. events.title: Demo update: bigger on wide monitors, and it gets further while you're away
events.summary: Two people told me the strip was too small to read on a wide monitor, and one of them said it was sitting on top of something they use all day. Both of those are fixed. Settings has a UI size option now. On a 1440p or ultrawide screen the game picks the larger size for you the first time you run it, and every window scales with it, not just the strip. There is an Always on top toggle if you would rather other windows cover it, and a Left, Center, Right setting for where it parks along the bottom

events.title: The Pocket Adventurer demo is live
events.summary: You can play it right now, free, for as long as you want. Pocket Adventurer sets up camp in a thin strip above your taskbar. Your hero trains, delves, and loots on their own while you work, study, or watch something. Click into camp when you want to; ignore it when you don't. The demo covers the first four dungeons, the camp, companion recruiting, and hero re-summoning, so you can see the whole shape of the game. The full game launches November 3 at $4.99.
